source: Standard geometry drawings RDM/1/3/2/01 (Junction type A) and RDM/1/3/2/02 (Junction types B, C & D), Jan 2024; markings to RDM 6.1 (2025) Chapters 5 and 7
note: Islands and markings for the user to place at a junction. Shapes follow the drawn dimensions where the sheets give them and are indicative elsewhere (the sheets are marked 1:500 but are not to scale). The control radii, entry widths W1/W2 and kerb lines come from the junction design, not from these templates: place a piece, then scale it, or move it, to fit. Kenya drives on the left: the approach lane of the minor road is on the right of a person looking up the minor road from the main road.

A-1.name: Junction type A-1 with two islands

A-2.name: Junction type A-2 with additional island

B-Mod.name: Junction type B, modified (ghost island on the main road)
B-Mod.remark: The sheet is titled types B, C and D but labels no panel D: two panels read 'Type B - Modified'. Both are drawn alike and are one template here.

SIG.name: Signalised crossroads (four arms, no islands)
SIG.remark: Not one of the RDM 1.3 templates: the geometric layout of a four-arm signal-controlled junction of single carriageways (RDM 6.1 7.8, Figure 7.12) - kerb returns, crossings, stop lines, centre lines and arrows. Signals, lane allocation and phasing come from the signals design (RDM 6.3).

DESC.name: Descending lane
DESC.remark: Where an upgrade warrants a climbing lane and is longer than 1000 m, the opposite side may be a candidate for a descending lane, especially with high traffic and slow trucks (RDM 1.3 6.6.4). Laid out as a climbing lane for the downhill traffic.

BCA.name: Brake check area
BCA.remark: Before a steep descent on routes with about 500 trucks a day: room for several semi-trailers, acceleration and deceleration tapers, good visibility and advance signs (RDM 1.3 12.5). Dimensions are indicative: RDM gives none.

RAMP.name: Truck escape ramp
RAMP.remark: Tangential to the carriageway on a tangent, before a singular point, after a 130 m vertical drop; 3.6-12 m wide; arrester bed length from Equation 12.1 and Table 12.7; bed up to 1.0 m deep tapered from 75 mm over the first 30-60 m; end mound 0.6-1.5 m, 1:1.5 slopes; signs E1, I33, I32 (RDM 1.3 12.7, RDM 6.2 6.7). Horizontal layout only: finish the ramp profile in Civil 3D.

TM07.name: GIVE WAY line, 600 / 300 mm, 400 mm wide

BM07.name: Triangular GIVE WAY marking, 3.75 x 1.1 m

LM24.name: Continuous centre line, 100 mm (barrier line on the minor road)

KERB.name: Raised island, kerbed (kerb faces marked black / white 500 mm, RDM 6.1 12)

GUIDE.name: Construction guide (not marked on the road)

LM05.name: Bay separation line, 1 m / 1 m, 200 mm (white)

LM03.name: Broken lane line 2 m / 6 m, 100 mm (white)

BAYEDGE.name: Edge of the widened pavement (no kerb shown on RDM/1/3/3/03)

SPLAY-A.name: Visibility splay, approach / give way (RDM 1.3 Figure 9.11)

SPLAY-S.name: Visibility splay, stop: always to be provided (RDM 1.3 Figure 9.12)

ACCESS.name: Private access formation edge with 6 m returns

PIPE.name: Traversable drainage pipe across the access (indicative)

RBEDGE.name: Roundabout outer kerb with entry and exit returns

APRON.name: Mountable apron edge around the central island

TM04.name: Broken line across the exit, 600 / 300 mm, 200 mm wide (white)

AM06.name: Right and left arrow (RDM 6.1 Table A.5)

AM07.name: Straight, right and left arrow (RDM 6.1 Table A.5)

SPLAY-M.name: Minor road approach visibility splay (RDM 1.3 Figure 9.13)

WIDEN.name: Widened carriageway edge for an island (guide for the corridor)

BM02.name: Pedestrian crossing blocks 3000 x 500 mm (RDM 6.1 Table A.4)

TM01.name: STOP line, continuous 400 mm (RDM 6.1 Table A.2)

ghost_island.name: Ghost island tail on the main road (hatched, yellow)
ghost_island.remark: Beyond the junction for the traffic turning right into the minor road; the right-turn lane length and the main-road widening come from the junction design (RDM 1.3 Fig 9.37).

ghost_lead.name: Hatched strip ahead of the right-turn lane (yellow)

splitter_a1.name: Splitter island, type A-1 (raised 7.5 x 3.0 m, R 1.5, hatched tail)

splitter_a2.name: Splitter island, type A-2 (raised teardrop, hatched tail, about 25 m)

splitter_teardrop.name: Splitter island, types B / C (teardrop 10 + 10 m, R 0.75)

corner_hatch.name: Hatched lead-in to the corner island (white)

give_way_line.name: GIVE WAY line across the approach lane (TM07)
give_way_line.remark: Across the approach lane from 'inner' (the splitter island's edge) to the kerb.

minor_centre_line.name: Continuous centre line on the minor road, 30 m (LM24)

guides.name: Guide lines: main edge, minor centreline and edges, kerb returns, Rc turning arcs
guides.remark: Construction only: no quantities. Kerb returns are three-centred curves R1 : R2 : R3 = 2 : 1 : 3 (RDM 1.3 Figure 9.25), R2 half the return radius within 8-12 m (set 'r2' to choose it, or 'three_centred': false for a single-radius fillet); Rc arcs are tangent to the main-road centreline and pass through the splitter nose; Rc is the control radius, 15 m recommended (RDM/1/3/2/01 note 1). On a corner with an island the return is drawn from the widened bellmouth, clear of the island by the turning roadway ('slip': 4.9 m in A-1, 5.5 m (W2) in A-2), with the widened edges tapering back over 'slip_taper' (30 m). The minor road's edges flare out by half the splitter's width around it ('minor_flare') and taper back, so its lanes keep their width.

bus_bay.name: Bus bay (RDM/1/3/3/01)
bus_bay.remark: Entry taper A = 30 m, 25 m where the speed limit is 50 km/h or less; bay B as clicked (25 m for more than one bus); exit taper C = 18 m; 4.0 m deep; 1.0 m raised platform; flush kerbs on the tapers, raised along the bay with 2 m ramped kerbs. Bays serving opposite directions at least 60 m apart, centre to centre.

truck_bay.name: Truck parking bay (RDM/1/3/3/03)
truck_bay.remark: Entry taper 15 m, bay 70 m (varies with the design), exit taper 10 m, straight tapers; 3.5 m deep; white separation line 1 m / 1 m, 0.2 m wide, along the carriageway edge from the start point to the end point. Room for four to five heavy vehicles, bays at most 30 km apart, not where visibility is restricted (RDM 1.3 13.2). Sign I15 at the start of the entry taper, I14 up to 500 m ahead (RDM 6.2 6.4.1.1).

climbing_lane.name: Climbing lane (RDM 1.3 6.6, RDM/1/3/3/02)
climbing_lane.remark: Tapers of 100 m; full width to where trucks are back within 15 km/h of their level speed, at least 200 m past the crest to merge; lane as wide as the adjacent through lane, which is reduced by 0.25 m where 3.25 m or more (RDM 1.3 6.6.3).

splays.name: Visibility splays (RDM 1.3 9.5.4)
splays.remark: Approach (give way) triangle: 20 m back from the main road's lane edge, Table 9.7 along the main road; stop triangle: 3 m back, Table 9.8. Both sides. Keep them clear of obstructions; at least the stop splays must always be provided.

access.name: Private access (RDM 1.3 9.11.16, Figure 9.33)
access.remark: Entry and exit radii 6 m or more for the expected turning traffic; at least 3 m wide (0.5 m shoulders as drawn); built back to the road reserve / boundary line, at least 10 m from the road edge, with a 3 m taper to match the existing access; a traversable drainage pipe as required; located to satisfy the stop-condition visibility (RDM 1.3 9.5.4, Figure 9.12; the text's 'Section 4.5' is a cross-reference slip).

roundabout.name: Roundabout (RDM 1.3 Chapter 10, RDM 6.1 Figures 7.14-7.16)
roundabout.remark: Centre on our road; arms where our road and other alignments cross the inscribed circle, plus clicked arms. Central island, outer kerb with entry / exit returns, kerbed splitter islands with hatched lead-ins, TM07 give way and BM07 triangle 2.5 m back on each entry, TM04 across each exit, LM24 on the approach (RDM 6.1 Figure 7.14). Signs: W17 on our approaches, R2 at each entry, M5 on each splitter nose, a W24 chevron on the central island facing each entry.

turn_arrow.name: Right-turn arrows in the right-turn lane (RDM 6.1 6.4.3)
turn_arrow.remark: Two AM03 arrows in the right-turn lane, the first 6 m before the junction point, 30 m apart; length from RDM 6.1 Table 6.1 at the main road's speed. Move them to the lane the junction design gives.

approach_arrows.name: Arrows on the minor road's approach (RDM 6.1 6.4.3)
approach_arrows.remark: AM06 (right and left) on the approach lane, its tip 10 m from the main road's edge; AM07 at a crossroads.

approach_splay.name: Minor road approach visibility splay (RDM 1.3 Figure 9.13)
approach_splay.remark: Where our road is the minor road: the sight lines from one stopping sight distance back to the give way line and its sign. Added with the splays when our road joins another road.

main_widening.name: Main road widening for the ghost island (lanes keep their width)
main_widening.remark: Both edges move out by half the ghost island's width over the right-turn lane and the island, tapering back; goes into the Widenings table for the Civil 3D corridor. Lengths indicative (RDM/1/3/2/01: 106 m approach taper); set them from the junction design.

signal_crossroads.name: Signalised crossroads: returns, crossings, stop lines, arrows (RDM 6.1 Figure 7.12)
signal_crossroads.remark: Four arms: kerb returns (guides, R 12 m), a BM02 crossing where the kerb runs straight, the TM01 stop line 1.5 m behind it across the approach half, 30 m of LM24 and an AM07 arrow on each approach.

descending_lane.name: Descending lane (RDM 1.3 6.6.4)
descending_lane.remark: Laid out as a climbing lane (RDM/1/3/3/02) for the downhill traffic: 100 m tapers, the lane as wide as the reduced through lane; I12 Slow Lane at its start.

brake_check.name: Brake check area (RDM 1.3 12.5)
brake_check.remark: Indicative: 100 m holds four to five semi-trailers, 60 m straight deceleration and acceleration tapers, 3.5 m deep; I14 500 m ahead, I15 at the entry taper, W30 where the descent starts.

escape_ramp.name: Truck escape ramp (RDM 1.3 12.7)
escape_ramp.remark: Departs tangentially on the downhill traffic's left at a small angle (4 deg here); the road edge widens to the ramp over a 50 m taper; 30 m of paved entry, then the arrester bed and a 'last chance' mound at the end. Bed length from Equation 12.1 for the runaway speed.
